type: pathway versus target under a tree model, plus an invalid first attempt

invalid_first_attempt.design: drug identity codes plus grouping codes fed to the tree
invalid_first_attempt.why_invalid: held-out drugs take integer code values unseen in training, so the tree routes them arbitrarily and identity scores 0.081 where it can carry no information

corrected.design: grouping codes only, no drug identity features

conclusion_1: the pathway-over-target ranking is model-independent: both groupings beat a random grouping and pathway beats target under both families

conclusion_2.why: the tree reaches 0.1074 with the grouping alone, close to ridge's 0.1254, whereas R138's tree reached only 0.032
conclusion_2.likely_cause: R138's tree carried drug identity codes that were all the reserved code -1 on the evaluation rows, a dead feature that consumes splits and distorts routing
conclusion_2.status: C106 must be re-tested with dead features removed before being quoted again

an_underpowered_intermediate.action: raised to 60 splits rather than reporting an underpowered null

recurring_failure_class.rule: before comparing arms, confirm that every feature present in every arm actually carries information in the evaluation condition

limits: Sixty splits and one untuned tree configuration.
Grouping codes are integer-coded rather than native categorical, so an encoding effect cannot be excluded.
Retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim.
next_gate: re-test C106 with the corrected design, no dead features on either side
